facts.claim: The 787-10 is the largest Dreamliner variant with the shortest range, with a maximum range of 7,500 nautical miles (13,890 km); in November Singapore Airlines will fly it on 26 routes for 1,129 operations and over 380,000 seats, with 337 seats per jet.

The ten shortest 787-10 routes in November all originate at Singapore Changi: Ho Chi Minh City 675 miles (30 operations), Surabaya 854 miles (60), Bangkok 876 miles (106), Bali 1,037 miles (60), Manila 1,474 miles (120), Hong Kong 1,587 miles (30), Guangzhou 1,638 miles (30), Colombo 1,709 miles (30), Dhaka 1,794 miles (30) and Chennai 1,817 miles (30).

Singapore Airlines' only narrowbody aircraft are 26 Boeing 737 MAX 8 jets seating 154 passengers, for a total capacity of 4,004, compared with 9,436 for its 28 Dreamliners; its fleet totals 165 aircraft including 65 A350s, 12 A380s, 27 777s and 28 787-10s.

The 787-10 configuration has 36 business class seats in a 1-2-1 layout and a 301-seat economy cabin with no premium economy; business class offers 60 inches of pitch and 20 inches of width and lies flat, while economy offers 32 inches of pitch, 17 inches of width and 5 inches of recline.

In November the 787-10 flies over 3,000 miles on four routes — Adelaide, Tokyo Narita, Chubu Centrair and Kansai — with Adelaide the longest at 3,351 miles and Kansai the highest-frequency at 90 operations and over 92 million available seat miles.

An FAA airworthiness directive covering all 787 variants takes effect next month because sealant defects could create a spark inside fuel tanks during a lightning strike; 60 of the 170 US-registered 787s fall under it, with inspections of 34 hours costing $2,890 per jet, and Singapore Airlines has an outstanding order for 31 Boeing 777X jets placed in June 2017 and February 2021.

zh.title: 新航為何拿787-10飛短程區域線？337席高密度機隊的算盤
zh.summary: 波音787-10是航程最短、載客最多的夢幻客機，新加坡航空卻拿它飛東南亞短程區域線：11月26條航線、1,129班次、逾38萬席，背後是僅26架737 MAX 8的窄體機隊撐不起區域運量，以及337席高密度布局的成本邏輯。
body: 波音787-10是夢幻客機家族中最大、航程最短的成員，最大航程7,500海里（13,890公里），仍足以執行傳統長程任務；新加坡航空卻把它用在另一種方向：飛那些通常屬於窄體客機的短程航線。依Cirium資料，新加坡航空11月將以787-10執飛26條航線，共1,129班次、逾38萬席，每架飛機載客337人；26條航線多數為區域線，航程不到787-10最大航程的三分之一。最短的10條航線全數自新加坡樟宜機場出發：胡志明市675英里（1,086公里）每月30班、泗水854英里（1,374公里）60班、曼谷876英里（1,410公里）106班、峇里島1,037英里（1,668公里）60班、馬尼拉1,474英里（2,372公里）120班、香港1,587英里（2,554公里）30班、廣州1,638英里（2,636公里）30班、可倫坡1,709英里（2,750公里）30班、達卡1,794英里（2,887公里）30班、清奈1,817英里（2,924公里）30班。

班次密度說明新航用夢幻客機在短距離上運送大量旅客的策略。其中最頻繁的是新加坡—馬尼拉線，11月120班、近6,000萬可用座位英里；新加坡—曼谷線106班、35,722席、逾3,100萬可用座位英里；最短的新加坡—胡志明市線每日1班、逾1萬席、680萬可用座位英里。背後是機隊結構：新加坡航空唯一的窄體客機是26架波音737 MAX 8，每架154席，總載客量4,004人，不到28架787-10總載客量9,436人的一半。依Planespotters.net資料，新航機隊共165架：A350共65架、平均機齡7.6年，A380共12架、12.8年，737共26架、4.9年，777共27架、14.1年，787-10共28架、5.9年，整體平均機齡9年。區域線需要的正是高載客量：東南亞各大城市人口密集，787-10一次可消化大量需求；相較之下，航程8,500海里（15,750公里）、可延伸至9,700海里（17,964公里）的A350-900，則被保留給長程與高收益航線。787-10客艙採高密度布局：商務艙36席、1-2-1配置，經濟艙301席、無特選經濟艙，僅一排經濟艙標示為加大腿部空間；商務艙椅距60英寸（152公分）、寬20英寸（51公分）、可全平躺，經濟艙椅距32英寸（81公分）、寬17英寸（43公分）、椅背傾斜5英寸（11.6公分）。

並非所有787-10航線都是短程。11月有4條航線超過3,000英里（4,830公里）：阿得雷德、東京成田、名古屋中部與大阪關西，其中只有阿得雷德在亞洲以外；最長的阿得雷德線3,351英里（5,400公里），11月52班、17,524席、5,870萬可用座位英里，新航2024年才慶祝進駐該市40週年、1984年首航時使用747執飛，A350亦自2023年10月起加入該航線；班次最多的長程線是關西，90班、30,330席、平均3,040英里（4,900公里）、逾9,200萬可用座位英里，是新航所有夢幻客機航線中最高者。風險也存在：美國聯邦航空總署一項涵蓋所有787機型的適航指令將於下月生效，原因是密封膠缺陷可能在閃電擊中時於油箱內產生火花，指令指出，若不處理此不安全狀況，可能在油箱容積內形成點火源；美國註冊的170架787中有60架適用該指令，每架檢查需34小時、費用2,890美元，新航的夢幻客機雖不在指令範圍內，但若問題遍及全球機隊仍可能受影響，全球787已逾1,100架。新航另有31架777X訂單待交付，2017年6月與2021年2月下訂、無選擇權，認證延宕已久，波音堅稱認證與交付終將於2027年實現；777X到位後，應可進一步鞏固新航以夢幻客機服務短程高運量航線的布局。

en.title: Why Singapore Airlines flies its Boeing 787-10s on short regional routes
en.summary: The Boeing 787-10 is the largest Dreamliner with the shortest range, yet Singapore Airlines uses it on short regional routes: 26 routes, 1,129 operations and more than 380,000 seats in November. The logic sits in a fleet with only 26 narrowbody jets and a 337-seat high-density layout built for moving large numbers of people.
body: Boeing built the 787-10 Dreamliner as the largest Dreamliner variant with the shortest range. With a maximum range of 7,500 nautical miles (13,890 km), it is still capable of traditional long-haul missions, but Singapore Airlines takes its 787-10s in a different direction, using them to fly short routes typically flown by narrowbody jets. Cirium data shows Singapore Airlines will fly the 787-10 on 26 routes throughout November, for a total of 1,129 operations and over 380,000 seats, with each jet carrying 337 passengers. The majority of these 26 routes are regional, coming in at less than a third of the 787-10's range. The ten shortest routes, all originating at Singapore Changi Airport (SIN), are Ho Chi Minh City at 675 miles (1,086 km) with 30 operations, Surabaya at 854 miles (1,374 km) with 60, Bangkok at 876 miles (1,410 km) with 106, Bali at 1,037 miles (1,668 km) with 60, Manila at 1,474 miles (2,372 km) with 120, Hong Kong at 1,587 miles (2,554 km) with 30, Guangzhou at 1,638 miles (2,636 km) with 30, Colombo at 1,709 miles (2,750 km) with 30, Dhaka at 1,794 miles (2,887 km) with 30, and Chennai at 1,817 miles (2,924 km) with 30.

These routes have impressive frequency, showing that Singapore Airlines uses its Dreamliners to move many people over short distances. The most frequent route is Singapore–Manila, with 120 monthly frequencies producing almost 60 million available seat miles; Singapore–Bangkok runs 106 times in November, offering 35,722 seats and over 31 million available seat miles, while the shortest route, Singapore–Ho Chi Minh City, operates daily with over 10,000 seats and 6.8 million available seat miles. The answer is also in Singapore Airlines' fleet, which lacks capacity for short-haul routes with other jets. Its only single-aisle aircraft are 26 Boeing 737 MAX 8 jets, each seating 154 passengers, for a total capacity of 4,004 passengers, compared with 9,436 for its Dreamliners. Using Planespotters.net data, the carrier's fleet totals 165 aircraft: 65 Airbus A350s with an average age of 7.6 years, 12 A380s at 12.8 years, 26 Boeing 737s at 4.9 years, 27 Boeing 777s at 14.1 years and 28 Boeing 787-10s at 5.9 years, for an overall average age of 9 years. The A350-900, with a range of 8,500 nautical miles (15,750 km) that can extend to 9,700 nautical miles (17,964 km), is instead kept for long-haul and premium-dense routes. The Dreamliner configuration is built for high-frequency, high-capacity needs: 36 business class seats in a 1-2-1 configuration and a 301-seat economy cabin, with no premium economy class and just one row marked as extra legroom. Business class seats offer 60 inches (152 cm) of pitch and 20 inches (51 cm) of width and lie flat, while economy offers 32 inches (81 cm) of pitch, 17 inches (43 cm) of width and 5 inches (11.6 cm) of recline.

Despite the prevalence of routes under 2,000 miles (3,200 km), some routes get closer to the typical way carriers use widebody aircraft. In November, Singapore Airlines will fly its 787-10s over 3,000 miles (4,830 km) on four routes: Adelaide (ADL), Tokyo Narita (NRT), Chubu Centrair (NGO) in Nagoya and Osaka Kansai (KIX). Only one of these routes takes the 787-10 outside Asia. The longest is Adelaide at 3,351 miles (5,400 km), flown 52 times in November for 17,524 seats and 58.7 million available seat miles; in 2024, Singapore Airlines marked 40 years in the city, having first flown there in 1984 using a 747, and the A350 also serves the route since October 2023. The highest-frequency route over 3,000 miles is Kansai, with 90 frequencies across November producing 30,330 seats at an average distance of 3,040 miles (4,900 km) and over 92 million available seat miles — the highest for any Singapore Airlines Dreamliner route. Risks remain: a Federal Aviation Administration airworthiness directive covering all 787 variants comes into effect next month, instituted because sealant defects could create a spark inside the fuel tanks during a lightning strike. "The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could result in development of an ignition source within the fuel tank volume," states the FAA order. The FAA says 60 of the 170 US-registered 787s fall under the directive, requiring sealant inspections where the wings meet the fuselage and adhesion checks, with the work for each jet at 34 hours and costing $2,890 per jet. Singapore Airlines' Dreamliners do not fall under this directive, but could be affected if a problem exists for Dreamliners worldwide; with over 1,100 Dreamliners worldwide, the problem could cause substantial disruption. Elsewhere in the fleet, Singapore Airlines has an outstanding order for 31 Boeing 777X jets, placed in June 2017 and February 2021, with no options. The family has been long-delayed by certification issues, although Boeing insists certification and deliveries will finally come in 2027; its arrival should further cement the need for Singapore Airlines to use its Dreamliners on short, high-capacity routes.
